I took Vinted to court to get my money back - BBC News
Image source,Mali OsmelakImage caption,
Mali Osmalek says she was stuck in a cycle of automated responses from Vinted
ByEmma Simpson,Business correspondentandDanielle Codd,Business reporter
Mali Osmelak never imagined that selling clothes on Vinted would end with a court claim to recover almost £6,000.
She started trading on the platform to earn an income while managing Crohn's disease and caring for her four-year-old daughter.
But when she became a professional seller in March, she was unable to complete Vinted's verification process, leaving thousands of pounds inaccessible in her Vinted wallet. After several weeks of trying to resolve the issue, Mali took legal action.
Vinted says sellers may be asked to complete verification checks to comply with legal and regulatory requirements and 98% of transactions are completed smoothly without needing help from its support team.
Vinted is hugely popular in the UK with 17 million users. The online marketplace does not charge a fee to sellers for listing on there.
After the BBC reported onusers whose accounts had been suspended or banned, dozens of people got in touch describing difficulties accessing money held in their Vinted wallets.
Mali joined Vinted in 2024 as a side-hustle. Demand for her second-hand gymwear grew rapidly and, within months, she had set up a limited company to expand the business.
This year she signed up for a Vinted Pro seller account - designed for people who want to sell a high volume of items and who are registered as a business.
Within weeks she had generated almost £6,000 in sales. But when she tried to withdraw the money, she discovered her account had been restricted and was told she needed to complete a verification process.
"I thought, 'That's OK. It's not rocket science,'" she says. "I'd set up the business with the help of an accountant and had all the information they needed."
Mali says she spotted an error Vinted had made with her name and she flagged it with Vinted, but "again nothing was done and the verification kept failing". She found herself stuck in a cycle of automated responses.
In an effort to break the deadlock, she also contacted Mangopay, the payments company that at the time operated Vinted sellers' wallets and processed transactions on the platform. She was directed back to Vinted.
After eight weeks without access to the money, Mali decided to take both companies to the small claims court, spending £455 in court fees.
Three days after the court claim was filed, Mali says the account was "magically verified" and she could withdraw the funds.
She still pressed ahead with the case though to try to recover her court fees, costs and interest.
In June, she obtained a default judgement after neither Vinted nor Mangopay responded to her claim, with the court ordering the companies to pay £1,207.50.
But she has yet to receive the money. She has since been informed that Vinted and Mangopay have applied to have the judgement set aside, with a hearing scheduled for December.
"It's been ridiculous and incredibly stressful," she says.
"I need that cash. I will fight it. I'm going to tell the court their system is completely broken. I needed help and nobody helped me."
Vinted said: "Ms Osmelak's check was not successful because her documents did not match the name on her Vinted account. We have since helped her update it, and her account is now verified."
The company did not respond to the BBC's questions about the legal action Mali has taken and continues to pursue.
Mangopay said it was "bound to professional secrecy and data protection obligations. We are, therefore, not allowed to comment on individual cases involving our clients or their users, nor can we share details about specific accounts, transactions or legal matters."
Image source,Azri MuktharImage caption,
Azri Mukthar says he has now stopped selling on Vinted
Sportswear seller Azri Mukthar told the BBC he has been trying to withdraw almost £2,500 from his account for over a year.
The businessman was more than happy to become a Pro seller as he was already registered as a limited company.
"I submitted all the documentation they requested and got the go-ahead from Vinted. So then I uploaded all the products and got 30 to 40 sales immediately," he says.
But when he wanted to withdraw his earnings, he found that he couldn't.
"They said my verification was pending," he says.
Azri shared a frustrated conversation he had with Vinted's AI assistant
Azri too, says he's been round in endless circles repeatedly submitting documents only to get an immediate response saying they had been rejected.
"It's frustrating and annoying as there's no clear system to follow.
"You contact customer support and they say you've not submitted X, Y or Z. But I know I have done all they're asking for."
He claims a certificate from Companies House that Vinted requested has been declined 15 times.
Azri has now stopped selling on Vinted and says he is going to have to start legal action.
Vinted said: "Mr Mukthar's check could not be completed because he did not provide all the required documents. Our support team is currently in touch with him to help with his verification."

lead_title: Jim Cramer says Anthropic's explosive growth could justify a record-breaking IPO

evidence_pages.https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/anthropi:
Anthropic IPO: Cramer on revenue growth and valuationSkip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
Jim Cramer said Anthropic's explosive revenue growth helps justify its record valuation.
"Anthropic's tantalizing growth rate is the key reason why this should be the largest IPO in history," Cramer said.
watch nowVIDEO3:5603:5647% sequential growth is still impressive, says Jim Cramer on AnthropicMad Money with Jim Cramer
Anthropic'sstunning revenue growth helps justify its $1 trillion-plus valuation ahead of what could become the largest initial public offering in history, CNBC'sJim Cramersaid Tuesday.
The Claude developer filed updated IPO paperwork Tuesday outliningplans to offer825 million shares at $70 to $78 apiece. At the high end, the offering would raise $64.35 billion andvalue Anthropic at up to $1.405 trillionon a fully diluted basis. The company plans to price its shares Nov. 18 and begin trading the following day. Throw in a separate $26 billion private placement purchased by leading AI companies includingNvidiaandAlphabet, and Anthropic's entire haul could exceed SpaceX's raise from its June IPO.
"The fact that this deal is on is bullish for tech and the AI trade," the "Mad Money" host said.
Anthropic reported $33.2 billion in revenue during the first nine months of 2026, up 1,206% from a year earlier, according to its updated prospectus. Much of that growth has been driven by enterprise customers, particularly surging adoption of Claude Code, its AI coding agent. "Anthropic's tantalizing growth rate is the key reason why this should be the largest IPO in history," Cramer said.
The company now has more than 11,900 customers spending over $100,000 annually, up from roughly 1,500 at the end of 2025. Existing customers are also spending dramatically more, with Anthropic reporting a net revenue retention rate of approximately 900% at the end of September, meaning customers are spending roughly nine times as much as a year earlier.
While Anthropic is seeing accelerating revenue growth through the first nine months of the year, the company's quarter-over-quarter growth rate seemed to peak in the second quarter, slowing to 47% in the third quarter from 144% in Q2. "To some extent, it's the law of large numbers at work, and let's be clear that 47% sequential growth is still very impressive," Cramer said.
While some deceleration is inevitable as the company gets larger, he said that increased competition from OpenAI and the possibility that customers are beginning to scrutinize their AI spending could also be factors. One thing is for sure, Anthropic won't have to jockey for position with OpenAI, which pushed its IPO plans into next year.
Additionally, Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate, which projects yearly revenue based on the most recent month's sales, suggests demand remains strong. The frontier AI lab reported an annualized revenue run rate of $81 billion at the end of October, putting the company within striking distance of $100 billion by year-end if its current momentum continues.
"It's good to see that it's still growing nicely," Cramer said. "As for Anthropic's revenue and growth rate, the main subject of tonight's review, it's nothing less extraordinary, even if we are slightly past the peak, growth-wise."

All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO | TechCrunch
Image Credits:Evan-Marie Petit PhotographyAI
All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO
Julie Bort11:57 AM PST · November 10, 2026
As Anthropic barrels toward an enormous IPO that could value it at$1.4 trillion,the company has disclosed a tidbit in its new S-1 filing about how many shares each of its seven co-founders plan to sell.
Each will sell 3,378,378 shares. Anthropic has floated an unusually broad initial price range of $70 to $78 a share. At the midrange of $74, each founder would take in just shy of $250 million.
At the low end, $70, each would have to settle for pocketing just over $236 million in cash; at the high end, $78, each would take in just under $264 million.
However, in an IPO as eagerly anticipated as this one, companies can often price shares above the initial range.
The S-1 is already hinting at high demand. Board member Reed Hastings has indicated he wants to buy $300 million worth of shares through his donor-advised fund. Board member Christopher Liddell also wants to buy $3 million worth of shares.
The seven co-founders are Dario Amodei, CEO; Daniela Amodei, president and chair of the board; Tom Brown, chief compute officer; Jack Clark, head of public benefit; Jared Kaplan, chief science officer (pictured above); Sam McCandlish, chief architect; and Christopher Olah, interpretability research lead.
After the sale, each of them will own about 3.2% of the total outstanding Class A shares, the S-1 says, or roughly 22% collectively. That’s not their share of the company overall. Class A is just one of Anthropic’s share classes, and other holders, including Amazon and Google, hold nonvoting Class N shares, so the founders’ stake in the company’s total equity will be considerably smaller. Even still, they, as a group, remain in control of the company. Each will also receive one share of Class F stock, which carries supervoting rights. Collectively, the founders will control 51.1% of the votes, but no single founder will hold significantly more shares or votes than the others.
As is now industry lore, the seven left OpenAI to start Anthropic in 2021 after disagreements with OpenAI’s leadership over how AI should be built. Siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, who held senior research and policy roles at OpenAI, were joined by five fellow OpenAI colleagues in forming a company that has said, very publicly and from the start, that it’s more focused on AI safety than its rivals, including the founders’ former employer.

These Xiaomi Phones Are No Longer Getting Support With The Latest HyperOS 4 Update
These Xiaomi phones are no longer getting support with the latest HyperOS 4 update
Xiaomi's new software has started rolling out in China, but older phones are being left behind.
ByLuke JamesNov. 10, 2026 6:00 pm ESTRoman Arbuzov/ShutterstockAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle Discover
Owners of a Xiaomi 17 in China are now receiving the latest HyperOS 4 update, which gives Xiaomi's software a new see-through look that's drawn plenty of comparisons to Apple's Liquid Glass. It began rolling out to the company's newest phones and tablets on October 15, 2026, but owners of the Xiaomi 12T and Redmi Note 12 are missing out. The update isn't coming to those models, which are already at, or are about to reach, the end of software support.
According to Xiaomi's official rollout schedule, the first batch of HyperOS 4 updates covers the Xiaomi 17 series, Redmi K100 and K90 series and the Xiaomi Pad 8, with more models following in waves through January 2027. Unfortunately, phones that are reaching the end of support this year, including the Xiaomi 12 and 12T, aren't on that schedule. Firmware trackers have also spotted a handful of cheaper models that, while still within their support windows, haven't been tested with HyperOS 4 at all. Xiaomi hasn't confirmed whether they'll miss out, though, and the rollout is only in China for now.
Xiaomi's schedule for its China firmware rollout lists 57 phones and 15 tablets in total. Following the first batch in mid-October 2026, the Xiaomi 17 Max, 17T and 17T Pro, Redmi K90 Max and Redmi Turbo 5 series were due by October 31, followed by the Xiaomi 15 series, MIX Flip 2, Civi 5 Pro and Redmi K80 series by November 15. The Redmi Note 17 and Note 15 lines come next, by November 30. December's batch is the biggest, taking in the Xiaomi 14 and 13 series, MIX Fold 3 and 4, Redmi K70 series and Redmi Note 14 Pro and 14 5G, while January 2027 is reserved for TVs and wearables.
A global beta opened in September 2026 for the Xiaomi 17, 17 Ultra and the Leica Leitzphone, followed by the 17T, 17T Pro, 15 and 15 Ultra, but Xiaomi hasn't yet provided a date for the global release.Beebomreported on October 11 that Xiaomi still hasn't confirmed a timeline for India or any other market, and Poco phones, which aren't sold in China, don't appear on the schedule at all.
Xiaomi publishes end-of-support dates on its security center site.Gizmochinahas counted 19 devices due to drop off in 2026. The Xiaomi 12 and 12 Pro, Redmi Note 12 5G, Redmi 12C and Redmi A2 and A2+ lost support in March, and the Poco F5 and F5 Pro in May. The Xiaomi 12T and 12T Pro reached the end of the line in October, followed by the Redmi 13C and Poco C65 in November. Once a model winds up on that list, it stops receiving OS upgrades and security patches entirely, so it's worth knowinghow to check if your Android phone is still getting security updates. Xiaomi's promises have gotten longer since, with the Xiaomi 15 getting four OS updates and six years of security patches, but that's still short of the seven years Samsung and Google now offer on their flagships.
Ximitime, which tracks Xiaomi's firmware, said there were no signs of HyperOS 4 test builds for any phone capped at Android 16. It named six models that hadn't entered testing: the Redmi Note 13 Pro 4G, Redmi Note 14S, Redmi A5 4G, Poco C71, Poco M6 Pro 4G and Poco X6 5G. Xiaomi hasn't confirmed that these phones are excluded, and some still have years of security updates left. If they are included, they'll stay on HyperOS 3.
Interestingly, the Xiaomi 13 series is on December's list, even though Xiaomi promised it three major Android updates, ending at Android 16, back in 2023. However, Xiaomi hasn't said whether its 13 series is getting Android 17 or a version of HyperOS 4 built on Android 16. With four years of security patches promised from its early 2023 global launch, the Xiaomi 13 is also now one of manypopular smartphones in their last year of software support.
Xiaomi calls the new design Soft Light Glass, a translucent material that it says adjusts its transparency based on the colors and content behind it. The lock screen's clock can now be resized, moved and restyled, much like the iPhones running iOS 26. Per Xiaomi, the full effect will only run on phones sporting a Snapdragon 8 Elite, Dimensity 9500 or Xiaomi's own XRING O1 chip or newer; older phones on the list get a simplified version.
Xiaomi also claims that HyperOS 4 leaves 27.2 percent more memory free after eight hours of use and opens apps 17.5 percent faster after long sessions. Meanwhile, its voice assistant, Super XiaoAI 2.0, now runs on Xiaomi's own MiMo AI model and adds an Expert Mode that can carry out multi-step tasks across apps, though most of the AI features are limited to China for now. HyperOS 4 is reportedly based on Android 17, but Xiaomi's newest phones already got Android 17 in July 2026 through an interim release called HyperOS 3.3.

Pixel phones getting new icon styles, Create My Widget, and more in November Pixel Drop - Ars TechnicaSkip to content
Text settingsStory textSizeSmallStandardLargeWidth*StandardWideLinksStandardOrange* Subscribers only
Google’s Pixel phones get an update every month, but most are just security patches and bug fixes. The bigger changes are bundled into quarterly Pixel Drops, and one isrolling out today. The update brings a few new things, and many of the Gemini features previously exclusive to the latest Pixel phones will also expand to Google’s Pixel 10 lineup.
The Pixel 11 was Google’s first foray into “Gemini Intelligence” branding, something we’ll see a lot more of going forward. Some of the features under that heading were limited to Google’s newest phones (and in some cases, Samsung’s phones). The November Pixel Drop will expand these AI features to the Pixel 10 lineup, but importantly, that doesn’t include the budget-orientedPixel 10a.
For starters, the Pixel 10 series will get the improved personalized suggestions (previously known as Magic Cue) that debuted on thePixel 11. This enables things like sending grocery lists to Google Keep from other apps and generating summaries from the context menu. Rambler, Google’s AI-assisted voice input system, is also coming to the 2025 phones. Likewise, Gemini app automation will roll out on Pixel 10 with this update. This feature is still limited to select apps in rideshare, food delivery, travel, and a few other categories.
The AI-powered icon theming that Google added to Pixels back in March is also getting an update. Initially, this feature just matched icon colors to the system theme when developers didn’t include the necessary theming assets. With this update, Google says it has moved the feature to a more powerful Nano Banana model, unlocking 10 new icon styles for your home screen.
The update also brings Create My Widget to Pixel phones. Google announced thisearlier in 2026, and itshipped on Googlebooksa few weeks ago. The idea is that you describe a home screen widget you want, and Android builds it for you on the spot. However, the use cases are pretty narrow. You’re limited to data accessible in search (e.g., stock prices, sports scores, and weather) and select Google account data points like Gmail or your calendar.
Left to right: Custom icons, Create My Widget, and Rambler.Credit: GoogleLeft to right: Custom icons, Create My Widget, and Rambler.Credit: Google
So that’s a lot of AI. Google does have some non-AI additions with this update, but don’t get your hopes up. One of the headlining additions is (drumroll) HiLight support for Google Messages. Yes, Pixel 11 phones will be able to illuminate HiLight when you get a message from important contacts. Ignoring that we had more functional notification LEDs 20 years ago, this is a good and necessary improvement for Google’s least useful hardware feature.
If you have a Pixel Watch, Google says this update will also improve your workout routine. The Pixel Watch 3 and newer will be able to display step-by-step guidance for your workouts. The wearable can also log reps and weights as you go without interrupting live metrics. While Create My Widget is not yet available on the watch, Google promises it’s also coming soon.
The update is beginning its rollout today and should be available widely in the coming days.

Free Chinese AI Models Are Getting Scary Good at Hacking | WIREDSkip to main content
Open-weight artificial intelligencemodels are now almost as capable ofhackinginto computer networks as the best closed ones, according to new research that heralds amuch-anticipated turning pointin the cybersecurity landscape.
Vals, a company that measuresAIcapabilities,set out to testhow well different AI models could carry out complex, multi-step network instructions on mock corporate networks.
“The best frontier models, locked up inside the labs and available only through trusted access programs, are now starting to be matched by open models that anybody can download,” says Nikil Ravi, a researcher at Vals.
The company’s findings suggest that closed models no longer have a definitive edge in cyber skills, meaning recent efforts by frontier labs to limit access to their models, and thereby slow the proliferation of such capabilities, may potentially be moot.
The findings are also noteworthy given that the US frontier labs, particularly Anthropic, premised thelimited release of new models—beginning withClaude Mythos Previewin April—on the idea that gated access would only buy time before advanced hacking capabilities were broadly available.
Anthropic's frontier red team lead, Logan Graham, told WIRED in April that the company’s Project Glasswing, which gives trusted access to the full capabilities of new models, was focused on getting those tools “in the hands of defenders to give a head start.”
“We need to prepare now for a world where these capabilities are broadly available in 6, 12, 24 months. Many things would be different about security,” he told WIRED at the time.
Seven months later, that transition seems to have arrived on schedule.
Vals tested AI models in two simulated scenarios, giving them various specific tasks to achieve. The first scenario involved a mock corporate network accessible through a public-facing website. The second involved two different company networks; a model needed to compromise the first in order to gain access to the second.
The researchers found OpenAI’s most advanced cyber model, Daybreak, which is available only to trusted partners, to be the most capable, completing 81 percent of the tasks it was given in an average of two tests. The Chinese open-weight model DeepSeek was not far behind, completing 73 percent of the objectives on average. The Vals researchers note that on some tasks, the two models scored equally.
The research also showed how much cheaper it is to use an open-weight model for this kind of task. Vals says it costs $17 to $46 in tokens for GPT-6-Sol to carry out an attack compared to $2 to $3 for DeepSeek. Open models are generally cheaper because they can be run on one’s own hardware. Rayan Krishnan, CEO of Vals, says this also provides a strong incentive for those playing defense to use open models rather than proprietary ones.
OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Much of the year in cybersecurity has played out as predicted, withAI automating core hacking tasksto helpboth attackers and defendersfind amassive number of new vulnerabilitiesin code and rapidly probe networks for weaknesses. While the speed and scale of the findings, and the intensity of fixing uncovered software flaws, have all increased, experts are still debating whether AI has fundamentally altered the conceptual foundation and tenets of cybersecurity defense. In other words, it’s still not clear whether AI tools pose a new kind of threat or amplify the security challenges that have long existed.
The fact that open-weight models are now starting to match closed ones is crucial for understanding how criminal hackers can harness AI, and how companies and developers should respond. But in practice, real-world observation of cybercriminal and state-backed hacking activity has repeatedly shown in recent months that attackers are doing what they always do by conserving their resources and generally making do with older and less capable models—both proprietary and open—for most of their activity. And even with strict controls, defenders must assume that the best-funded and most highly motivated attackers have already had at least some access to closed models all this time.
“I am in general agreement that open-weight models are capable of producing advanced attacks and vulnerabilities today, especially when you consider the abliterated models that disable safety training by modifying weights,” says Alex Zenla, cofounder and chief technology officer of the cloud security firm Edera. “My caveat to this is that it is likely that the closed labs have trained additional, unreleased models exceeding these capabilities. So I would put this very much like a cat-and-mouse game. The labs see themselves as moving fast to outpace the open-weight models, to be able to secure vulnerabilities before the open-weight models find them. Unfortunately, I do think this may be the beginning of a dangerous security landscape.”

What’s the point? Ten years after the Paris treaty, are climate talks getting anywhere?
Its key temperature goal has been missed but experts say the agreement is still proving a vital moral compass for progress
It was a curious way of conducting negotiations. Ahead of the 2025 climate summit, in the Amazonian port of Belém last year, the Brazilian hosts had taken off the table the issue that most had assumed would be at its heart: concrete plans from each country laying out exactly what they would be doing to cut their greenhouse gas emissions.
Brazil was insisting, instead, that these plans – the bedrock of the Paris agreement – were the business of national governments and not up for negotiation. “In that case, it will be a very short Cop,” one seasoned global south negotiator told the Guardian shortly before, reflecting a widespread unease. “There is nothing to negotiate.”
“They have decided that there is no appetite for negotiation, with the US out of Paris,” said another developing country diplomat. “Countries won’t engage.”
The summit ended with a deal, although few loved it. But, as the faultlines from the Brazilian decision deepen going into this year’s summit, it is clear that the Paris agreement, and climate action around the world, has reached an impasse.
View image in fullscreenAndré Corrêa do Lago, Cop30 president, sits as Simon Stiell, UN climate chief, left, speaks with other officials at Cop30 in Belém. The summit in Brazil ended with a deal that few loved.Photograph: André Penner/AP
And it is not just Cop insiders who are worried. For many outside the vast white air-conditioned conference halls, the question, as this year’s summit begins, will be: what is the point?
Those same governments have pledged year after year since the Paris agreement was signed in 2015 – and entered into force a year later – to limit global heating to 1.5C above preindustrial levels. Yet temperatures for two years have exceeded that threshold, and the UN revealed a few weeks ago that its most optimistic estimate wasnow for about 1.7 to 1.8C of heating.
There could be no clearer evidence that the Paris agreement, on the face of it, has failed. It is impossible not to wonder whether the Cop process itself is just not fit for purpose.
The charge sheet against Paris is long, with the central issue being the failure to achieve its goal. Beyond that immediate failure, the negotiation processes are endlessly convoluted and cause their own problems. It took more than five years just to negotiate the Paris “rulebook” under which the treaty is interpreted and put into effect.
The convention that all resolutions must pass by consensus has given bad actors free rein. Donald Trump’s allies – in Saudi Arabia, Russia, Venezuela and some other petrostates – frequently veto measures andobstruct progress.
It took more than 30 years of negotiation since the UN framework convention on climate change was signed in 1992 for fossil fuels even to be addressed directly. This was atCop28 in Dubai in 2023, where countries agreed for the first time to“transition away from fossil fuels”but failed to set a timeframe or any policies to back up the resolution.
View image in fullscreenAn oil spill at Lake Maracaibo in Bachaquero, Venezuela. Crude oil leaks devastate fishing communities, coat wildlife and cause severe ecological degradation around the lake.Photograph: Henry Chirinos/EPA
The US, the world’s biggest economy and responsible for about one in every eight tonnes of carbon dioxide emitted today, has withdrawn from Paris under President Trump.
Even parts of the developed world which support the process have mostly failed to come up with convincing plans: Australia, co-host of Cop31, has set no end to fossil fuel exports; its fellow co-hostTurkeyplans to increase its carbon output. The UK is opening a gasfield and mulling a new oilfield, Germany has dropped its electric vehicle sales targets and scrapped a renewable heating law. Meanwhile, most rich countries are reducing their contributions to climate finance for the poor.
Most of all, the slow pace of the Paris timetable might have seemed fine in 2015, when temperatures were rising at 0.2C a decade. Today, the rate of rise is 0.4C a decade and still accelerating.
“The structures of Cops and Paris are labyrinthine, bureaucratic, and ultimately dispiriting,” said Paul Bledsoe, a former Clinton White House climate adviser, now with the American University. “It may be time to streamline them to focus more deliberately on national emissions reduction goals.”
As ordinary people watch these failures outside and inside the process, some are losing faith. The Paris agreement was a sensation, celebrated around the world. In the years since, the aura of Cop has faded, as meetings seem to disintegrate into arguments over wording and compromise.
“A lot of the commitments, the promises that were made, just turned out to be a bunch of hot air,” said Juan Carlos Monterrey, former climate envoy for Panama, now chief executive of the Vanglabs consultancy. “Under that measure, we have failed.”
View image in fullscreenProtesters clash with security forces in an attempt to storm the Cop30 headquarters in Belém in 2025.Photograph: Andre Coelho/EPA
Johan Rockström, director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, said: “The fact that global warming is accelerating, that we inevitably will be breaching the 1.5C limit within three to five years, that tipping points are coming closer fast, that Earth’s resilience is showing worrying signs of decline, and that we still allow ourselves to follow a global path that will take us to a catastrophic 2.6C-3C, and that this is allowed to happen within the framework of the Paris agreement, cannot be considered as anything but a global failure.”

iFixit Teardown Shows How Apple's Glowing PROLED MacBook Logo Works
iFixit teardown shows how Apple's glowing PROLED MacBook logo works
The new laptop goes the extra mile to recreate the iconic feature.
ByIan Carlos CampbellNov. 10, 2026 7:03 pm ESTiFixitAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle Discover
iFixithas sharedits teardown ofApple's first touchscreen MacBook Proand besides bemoaning the company's half-hearted commitment to user repairability, it also showed off the physical components that make the laptop's glowing logo work. The new lid design is one of the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display's many charms, alongside its tandem OLED display and lighter weight.
Older LCD MacBooks featured a physical cutout that let the display's backlight illuminate the logo, but since OLED screens don't require backlights, Apple had to come up with a different solution to bring the design element back. iFixit found that the company uses a light strip with four LEDs layered behind the display, whose light is reflected through a diffuser to illuminate the logo. The Apple logo itself is also coated "like a two-way mirror," according to iFixit, so that it can appear metallic and reflective when the logo is off, but still let light through when the LEDs are on.
Appleditched the glowing logoin 2016, so it's a bit ironic that the company waited until it stopped using backlit displays to bring it back. It used to be a cool bit of branding before, but now the company may see the glowing logo design as an important way to distinguish its most expensive laptop from the kind we peons are forced to use.
The rest of the internal changes to the laptop are more expected. Apple was able to achieve the new MacBook Pro's lighter weight by using less aluminum in the base and lid of the laptop and including a slightly smaller trackpad. The laptop's hinge was also reworked to make the display wobble less when you tap the screen. Those changes don't make it any easier to fix, though. The laptop is still complex to disassemble: For example, iFixit says that you have to remove the laptop's logic board to switch out its USB-C ports. Plenty of other components, like the MacBook's memory and the HDMI port, are also soldered in place. Anyone droppingup to $15,000on a laptop probably isn't worried about doing their own repairs, but Apple's thin and light (and glowing) design comes with some tradeoffs, as always.

Review: Apple's M6 MacBook Pro is good, but it's missing all the exciting stuff - Ars TechnicaSkip to content
Text settingsStory textSizeSmallStandardLargeWidth*StandardWideLinksStandardOrange* Subscribers only
I’ve writtenmore than onceabout the weird positioning of Apple’s entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro, which has always occupied an uncomfortable perch between the MacBook Air and the higher-end MacBook Pros. The best versions of this laptop, like last year’s M5 refresh, come with the same basic design and external features of the higher-end MacBook Pros, just with a more modest processor and a lower ceiling for specs like RAM and storage.
The lesser versions stick with older designs or other compromises, reserving Apple’s most updated designs and screen technologies for the more expensive high-end models. Recall the 13-inch M1 and M2 MacBook Pros, which stuck with Apple’s 2016-era MacBook Pro designs foreverything, up to and including the now-abandoned Touch Bar. (If you’re someone at Apple maintaining Touch Bar support into the 2030s for the sake of these two laptop models, I’d like to hear from you. Not for a story! I’d just like to know how you are.)
This year’s entry-level MacBook Pro mostly falls into that latter category. Itdoesget an Apple M6 chip, and the M6 is great—rumors suggest the M6 won’t get Pro, Max, or Ultra configurations, so there are some fringe benefits here that youcan’tget in the top-tier MacBook Pros. But it uses the same MacBook Pro design Apple has been usingsince 2021. There’s no touchscreen, no OLED panel, no Dynamic Island, no half-pound weight reduction, no glowing Apple logo on the lid.
In other words, it has very little of what makes the “PROLED XDR” MacBook Pros interesting, despite starting at an objectively very high starting price of $1,999. This is $700 more than the basicM1 MacBook Profrom 2020 and$400 morethan the starting price of the M5 MacBook Pro from a year ago (though that model also got a mandatory 1TB storage upgrade and a $400 price hike when Appleraised most of its prices back in June).

fact_units.text: iFixit Teardown Shows How Apple's Glowing PROLED MacBook Logo Works
The new laptop goes the extra mile to recreate the iconic feature.
10, 2026 7:03 pm ESTiFixitAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle Discover

iFixithas sharedits teardown ofApple's first touchscreen MacBook Proand besides bemoaning the company's half-hearted commitment to user repairability, it also showed off the physical components that make the laptop's glowing logo work.
The new lid design is one of the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display's many charms, alongside its tandem OLED display and lighter weight.

Older LCD MacBooks featured a physical cutout that let the display's backlight illuminate the logo, but since OLED screens don't require backlights, Apple had to come up with a different solution to bring the design element back.
iFixit found that the company uses a light strip with four LEDs layered behind the display, whose light is reflected through a diffuser to illuminate the logo.

The Apple logo itself is also coated "like a two-way mirror," according to iFixit, so that it can appear metallic and reflective when the logo is off, but still let light through when the LEDs are on.
Appleditched the glowing logoin 2016, so it's a bit ironic that the company waited until it stopped using backlit displays to bring it back.
It used to be a cool bit of branding before, but now the company may see the glowing logo design as an important way to distinguish its most expensive laptop from the kind we peons are forced to use.
The rest of the internal changes to the laptop are more expected.
Apple was able to achieve the new MacBook Pro's lighter weight by using less aluminum in the base and lid of the laptop and including a slightly smaller trackpad.
The laptop's hinge was also reworked to make the display wobble less when you tap the screen.
Those changes don't make it any easier to fix, though.
The laptop is still complex to disassemble: For example, iFixit says that you have to remove the laptop's logic board to switch out its USB-C ports.
Plenty of other components, like the MacBook's memory and the HDMI port, are also soldered in place.
Anyone droppingup to $15,000on a laptop probably isn't worried about doing their own repairs, but Apple's thin and light (and glowing) design comes with some tradeoffs, as always.

The lesser versions stick with older designs or other compromises, reserving Apple’s most updated designs and screen technologies for the more expensive high-end models.

Jessica Pegula celebrates her victory over Marta Kostyuk at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, California, on Tuesday.Photograph: Matthew Stockman/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJessica Pegula celebrates her victory over Marta Kostyuk at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, California, on Tuesday.Photograph: Matthew Stockman/Getty Images
Noskova beats Gauff to reach WTA Finals semi-finals as Pegula stays alive
Czech defeats Gauff 6-3, 6-3 to reach last four
Pegula eliminates Kostyuk with straight-sets victory
Gauff and Pegula remain in contention for final berth
Linda Noskova secured her place in the semi-finals of the WTA Finals with a 6-3, 6-3 victory overCoco Gauffon Tuesday, while Jessica Pegula knocked Marta Kostyuk out of the season-ending tournament with a straight-sets win.
The Czech, who beat Kostyuk in her opening match, has won both encounters without dropping a set and is assured of advancing to the knockout stage. Gauff and Pegula are both 1-1, with the final round-robin matches on Thursday set to determine who joins Noskova in the last four.
Hot mics, Andreeva ‘diva’ drama and a stopgap finale at Indian Wells bail out the WTA | Tumaini CarayolRead more
Pegula earlier bounced back from her opening defeat to Gauff with a 6-2, 7-5 victory over Kostyuk, eliminating the Ukrainian from semi-final contention.
The American made a strong start, breaking Kostyuk in the opening game and securing another break to claim the first set. She carried that momentum into the second, breaking again at the start before the pair exchanged breaks twice.
Kostyuk’s mistakes undermined her attempts to fight back, with the Ukrainian committing 17 unforced errors in the opening set compared with Pegula’s three.
“Once I got off to a good start today, I definitely didn’t want to give away that second set,” Pegula said. “In general I wouldn’t want to, but I think it was a bit of an extra push to be able to give myself the best chance in this group, considering I did lose the first match.”
Noskova then took control against Gauff in a match marked by inconsistent serving from both players. The pair traded breaks at the start of the first set, but Noskova broke twice more to take the opener.
Gauff struggled to find consistency on serve again in the second set, allowing Noskova to build a 3-0 lead. The American fought to stay in the contest but could not find a way back, as Noskova held serve throughout the remainder of the set before sealing the win with an ace.
The result sends the Wimbledon champion into the semi-finals on her debut at the tournament, while Gauff will have another chance to qualify when she faces Kostyuk on Thursday. Pegula takes on Noskova in the other final Group 1 match.
Kostyuk, who replaced world No 1 Elena Rybakina after the Kazakh withdrew with a viral illness, is making her first appearance at theWTA Finals.
“I saw that she’s changing pace a lot, and I would struggle sometimes,” Kostyuk said after her defeat to Pegula. “Overall, I think I was pretty happy with my return today. You can obviously be better, everything can be better. Next time, maybe I’ll be more ready.”

WTA Finals: Linda Noskova beats Coco Gauff to reach semi-finals, Jessica Pegula wins - BBC Sport
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Linda Noskova won the Berlin Open before triumphing at Wimbledon a few weeks later
ByAmy LofthouseBBC Sport Senior Journalist
Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova dismantled Coco Gauff to become the first player to reach the last four of the WTA Finals.
Czech Noskova played with controlled aggression and served brilliantly to beat the American 6-3 6-3.
World number eight Noskova was composed throughout and broke Gauff's serve four times in the first set alone.
She sent powerful winners to all corners to outmuscle her opponent, who is one of the best movers on the WTA Tour, and committed only one unforced error in a dominant second set.
The 21-year-old fittingly sealed victory with an ace to secure a place in the semi-finals on her tournament debut.
"Thank you guys for the cheers I'm getting now - but it was a little weaker in the match, guys, I'm not going to lie," Noskova joked to the California crowd afterwards.
"I feel like I stayed in the match through every moment, from beginning to end."
It is a sixth top-10 victory of the season for Noskova, whowon her maiden Grand Slam at Wimbledonin July.
Gauff, whowon a thrilleragainst compatriot Jessica Pegula on Sunday, had a poor day on serve.
She hit the same amount of aces and double faults - eight apiece - and won only six of 24 points behind her second serve.
Fourth-ranked Gauff can still qualify for the last four, as can Pegula.
Earlier in group one, Pegula claimed her first win since September to eliminate alternate Marta Kostyuk.
American Pegula won 6-2 7-5 in a scrappy match that saw seven breaks of serve.
Ukraine's Kostyuk, who has been dealing with a wrist injury since August, only found out she would be playing on Saturday after world number one Elena Rybakina withdrew.
She lost her opener to Noskova on Sunday and struggled for rhythm and consistency in a low-quality match against Pegula.
Pegula made only five unforced errors to Kostyuk's 17 as she took the first set, and the home favourite quickly went up a break in the second.
However, four breaks of serve then ensued, with Pegula eventually sealing the decisive break at 5-5 before serving out victory.
Elsewhere, Britain's Toby Samuel fell 6-1 6-4 to world number 25 Lorenzo Musetti in the Basel Open second round.

Steve Smith and David Warner were sanctioned for their roles in the sandpaper scandal, a story that continues to rumble on eight years later.Photograph: Marty Melville/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSteve Smith and David Warner were sanctioned for their roles in the sandpaper scandal, a story that continues to rumble on eight years later.Photograph: Marty Melville/AFP/Getty Images
Cricket Australia wants to move on from ball tampering saga but its equivocation has the opposite effect
The interminable sandpaper scandal will drag on to the next press conference, social media post or book, until it festers into something much bigger than it needs to be
There are some stories that you look back on and wonder whether we lost our collective minds. In Australia, 2018 was not a good year for banking executives, for prime ministers, for oily lord mayors and for cardinals. But the greatest betrayal of trust apparently concerned our national cricket team. There was public bawling, righteous indignation, weasel words and sanctimonious pieties. Prime minister Malcolm Turnbull, flanked by a doleful Angus Taylor and a nodding firefighter, called it a “terrible disgrace”. “They now have to make sure this great national game, this great international game that is synonymous with fair play, is once again played by champions that everybody can look up to.”
Mitchell Starc breaks silence to deny knowledge of ball tampering planRead more
Turnbull was more of a sailing man anyway. His parliamentary tenure was the political equivalent of Graeme Hick’s cricket career. By the time he’d been punted from office four months later, the Australian cricket team was being reimagined. The Ethics Centre’s 116-page document used the “Everest Process” to ascertainCricketAustralia’s alignment with its ethical framework. There were lots of charts asking how well CA was adhering to this value or that. “Mostly not lived”, “sometimes lived” and “always lived” were some of the measures. One could have saved a lot of time, money and paper and simply concluded “don’t be a prick, don’t bark like a dog when an opponent is dismissed, and don’t shove sandpaper down your dacks”.
We sniggered at the “elite honesty” and the “compete with us, smile with us, dream with us” nonsense. But it cut to the core of what this issue was about – for the majority, it was less about whether they had cheated, and more about the kind of team they had become. Anyone who had played park, grade, shield or Test cricket had a sense of where ball tampering lay on the scale of atrocities. The loudest voices, whether they were PMs, radio hosts or bandana-clad opinionists, were those who had never played cricket at any level.
But people were fed up with that Australian side. The impression leading into the South Africa series was of a mean, cosseted, overworked, joyless team. It wasn’t helped by the baiting tabloids, the appalling TV coverage, the puerile marketing and the blind-eyed administration.
View image in fullscreenComposite: Sky Sports/Getty
But the odd dick pick and stumping incident aside, there was very little scandal with the post sandpaper-gate team. The appointment of Pat Cummins as captain was central to that. “No sledging, no arguing, no anger, no love gone wrong, no dust ups, no bust ups,” Peter Lalor wrote in The Australian. The usual grifters and chuckle merchants said he was too woke, and that the team was too nice. Where was the mongrel? Where was the mental disintegration? Meanwhile, the team met every challenge, quietly disabusing the idea that cricket was somehow central to the national psyche, and that they had to behave like complete assholes to be successful at it.
But the events in Cape Town were always bubbling away. “What’s left to come out after eight years?” Mitchell Starc asked on the eve of this year’s South African tour. Plenty, as it turns out. No-one, with the possible exceptions of Enid Blyton and Peter FitzSimons, write more books than Australian cricketers. And the literary ambitions of Usman Khawaja and David Warner were always going to further fan the flames. Hell, these days you don’t even need a book deal. You just need sufficient distance from national duties and functioning wifi. Warner’s thoughts were posted from Nepal, taking time out from demolition duties at the Kathmandu Gorkhas.
Khawaja has been accused of having an axe to grind, and a publishing fortune to make. One particularly objectionable columnist wrote of “his talent for inserting race, religion and victimhood into his story”. But the chapter on Cape Town isn’t as inflammatory as many have made out. The most interesting and revelatory passages in the book lie elsewhere. It did however address something that has never been properly examined, resolved or reckoned with. The initial press conference was a shambling, fudging, lying shambles. The subsequent investigation was wholly unsatisfactory. In a way it was understandable, though not necessarily forgivable. There were careers, reputations and relationships at stake. The imperative, just as it was with the AFL’s supplements and racism scandals, was for everyone to move on as quickly as possible.
The saga that never goes away: wounds of Australian cricket reopened as ball tampering resurfaces | Jack SnapeRead more
That was the crux of what Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg said on SEN this week – that it was a different administration, a different team, and a different time. “There were a lot of learnings that came out of it,” he said. There were echoes there of another CA boss, James Sutherland, who described the cricket as “an issues-rich environment”.
LinkedIn-speak like that is not only evasive, but represents a missed opportunity. Khawaja’s book provided the perfect chance for those directly involved and those who inherited this mess to be upfront about what happened, to explore the tissue-thin difference between intricate knowledge and collective responsibility. Australia fast bowler Mitchell Starc has denied any prior knowledge of 'Sandpapergate' after former team-mate Usman Khawaja's explosive claims that the entire dressing room knew about the ball-tampering scheme in South Africa in 2018.
Khawaja made the revelationsin his new book 'Sabr', bringing the scandal back onto the agenda after eight years.
David Warner -who said on Monday that Khawaja's version of events was "100 per cent accurate"- then captain Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were banned after the sandpaper affair, with Cricket Australia asserting only that trio were privy to the plot to alter the condition of the ball in order to try and make it swing.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, afterCricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg insisted there would be no re-opening of the 'Sandpapergate' investigation, Starc said of Khawaja's claims: "I haven't really paid much attention to it to be fair.
"There are differing opinions of eight years ago. We were heavily grilled through the process, at the time and since.

"As far as our statement said, we weren't aware of things being taken on the field. That's where I'll leave it.
"I will be sticking to what I said five years ago, what I said at the time eight years ago, so clearly there is differing versions from different people.
"We weren't aware of anything taken on the field to be tampered with. We saw it on the big screen in Cape Town.

On Khawaja saying the ball was also tampered with in the Test before the Cape Town fixture, at Port Elizabeth, now Gqeberha, Starc added: "That's the first I was aware of any of that."
Healy: Timing of Khawaja comments 'a little bit sticky'
Starc's wife, former Australia captain Alyssa Healy, addressed the fallout on theKeepin' it Cricketpodcast after Khawaja insisted he had not "thrown anyone under the bus", with the 36-year-old calling the timing of his comments "sticky".
Healy said: "Been scraping off bits of Mitch off the bitumen after the bus had just hit him over the last two days.
"I'm obviously in quite a unique predicament: I'm working in the media, I have to comment on these things [and] I'm also married to one of the players who is still playing who was there in that series and experienced all of that eight years ago.

"It's a hard one for me to comment on. I'm kind of going to sit back and watch it unfold I think, first and foremost, but what I will say is that the timing of it is just a little bit sticky for me. I don't like that."

The top cricket official in Australia has ruled out another investigation into the so-called “sandpapergate” scandal despite remarks by Usman Khawaja andDavid Warnerthat knowledge of the 2018 ball-tampering plot was widespread throughout the team.
Cricket Australia (CA) ⁠boss Todd Greenberg said on Tuesday he believed all players held “very different views” fromKhawaja’s version of eventsof the 2018 tour of South Africa as described in his recently released autobiography.
“There are specific details in his ⁠book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others,” Greenberg told ⁠local radio station SEN.
“But we have said we’re comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we’ve received,” he added.
“That includes what we’ve seen from Usman, and our position hasn’t changed on that. We don’t see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again. I don’t think ‌there’s anything that can be gained from that.”
CA imposed bans and other penalties on Warner, former captain Steve Smith and former Test batter Cameron Bancroft four days after the incident came to light during the Cape Town Test.
Khawaja, in extracts from his autobiography published in Australian media, said “open, lighthearted discussions” were held during the South Africa series about ways to scuff up the ball, including by using sandpaper.
He said discussion of tampering was not confined to batters, bowlers or staff but extended throughout the team.
“It was all of us,” Khawaja said in the book, ⁠according to Australian media.
Warner, who retired from international cricket more than two years ago, ⁠broke his silence about the incident on Monday to throw his support behindKhawaja.
In a video posted on social media, Warner described his former teammate’s account as 100 percent accurate and the CA investigation as “botched” and “rushed”.
The four Australian bowlers who played in the Cape Town Test in 2018 and continue to represent the nation – Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon – issued a joint statement in 2021 denying any knowledge of the plot.
Captain Cummins said in South ‌Africa last month that he had spoken to Khawaja about his autobiography and was not concerned about any potential fallout.
“Answered every question a million times. So, yeah, it was dealt with then,” he said.
Some commentators have questioned why Khawaja ‌waited ‌eight years to speak out and accused him of trying to boost sales of his book Sabr.
Khawaja responded on social media on Tuesday, saying he had no commercial motives.
“I’m very fortunate, I don’t need the money,” he said.

Michael Clarke played 394 matches for Australia between 2004 and 2015, captaining the Test side from 2011 until his retirement
Former Australia captain Michael Clarke has said fans of the national side "can't trust what's real" and has called for the investigation into the 2018 Australia ball-tampering scandal to be reopened.
Clarke's former international team-mate Usman Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about the use of sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball in the third Test against South Africa.
The incident led to bans for captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft, but a Cricket Australia investigation found the national side's bowling attack were unaware of the ball-tampering.
Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg, speaking before Clarke's intervention, said he does not see "any compelling reason" to reopen the investigation.
However Clarke said Australian fans "have not moved on" and that the investigation process needs to be restaged.
"They can't trust what's real. They don't know the truth until this gets reopened and the truth comes out," Clarke told 2DayFM.
"We had the chance in 2018. The truth didn't come out. We had the chance in 2021 when [Bancroft] made those comments. The truth didn't come out.
"Now we've got this opportunity. I would just like to see whatever the truth is for it all to come out, allow people to finally tell the truth, and move on."
Khawaja’s ‘sandpapergate’ revelations

In a 2021 interview with the Guardian, Bancroft was asked if the bowlers knew and replied: "It's pretty probably self-explanatory."
Shortly after Bancroft's interview, Australia's bowling attack in the contentious 2018 Cape Town Test issued a joint statement saying they "did not know a foreign substance was taken on to the field".
Pat Cummins featured in that line-up and Clarke said the current Australia Test captain needed to speak on Khawaja's allegations.
"For me, right now, there's more questions than answers," Clarke added.
"I want to know, firstly, did everyone know? Because certain players have come out and said they didn't. I want to know: did they know or not? That's important information so we can get the truth.
"I can't believe we haven't heard from Pat Cummins yet, the Australian captain. Steve Smith lost his job. If this doesn't happen, Tim Paine never captains Australia. And neither does Pat Cummins.
"Pat Cummins would not have captained a game at this stage if 'sandpapergate' didn't happen because Steve Smith would still be captain."
Smith lost his job as Australia captain after receiving a year-long ban for the sandpaper incident and was replaced by Paine. Cummins then took over the Test captaincy in November 2021.
Greenberg said he had not read Khawaja's autobiography in which his claims are made, but said he hoped to do so and that he had "huge respect" for the former batter giving "his version of events".
"There are specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others," Greenberg told Sports Entertainment Network.
"I want to be really careful to consider what Usman's actually said, and not respond to the headlines or the subsequent commentary that gets created.

"We have said we're comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we've received. That includes what we've seen from Usman, and our position hasn't changed on that.

Steve Smith and David Warner were sanctioned for their roles in the sandpaper scandal, a story that continues to rumble on eight years later.Photograph: Marty Melville/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSteve Smith and David Warner were sanctioned for their roles in the sandpaper scandal, a story that continues to rumble on eight years later.Photograph: Marty Melville/AFP/Getty Images
Cricket Australia wants to move on from ball tampering saga but its equivocation has the opposite effect
The interminable sandpaper scandal will drag on to the next press conference, social media post or book, until it festers into something much bigger than it needs to be
There are some stories that you look back on and wonder whether we lost our collective minds.
In Australia, 2018 was not a good year for banking executives, for prime ministers, for oily lord mayors and for cardinals.
But the greatest betrayal of trust apparently concerned our national cricket team.
There was public bawling, righteous indignation, weasel words and sanctimonious pieties.
Prime minister Malcolm Turnbull, flanked by a doleful Angus Taylor and a nodding firefighter, called it a “terrible disgrace”.
“They now have to make sure this great national game, this great international game that is synonymous with fair play, is once again played by champions that everybody can look up to.”
Mitchell Starc breaks silence to deny knowledge of ball tampering planRead more
His parliamentary tenure was the political equivalent of Graeme Hick’s cricket career.
By the time he’d been punted from office four months later, the Australian cricket team was being reimagined.
The Ethics Centre’s 116-page document used the “Everest Process” to ascertainCricketAustralia’s alignment with its ethical framework.
There were lots of charts asking how well CA was adhering to this value or that.
“Mostly not lived”, “sometimes lived” and “always lived” were some of the measures.
One could have saved a lot of time, money and paper and simply concluded “don’t be a prick, don’t bark like a dog when an opponent is dismissed, and don’t shove sandpaper down your dacks”.
We sniggered at the “elite honesty” and the “compete with us, smile with us, dream with us” nonsense.
But it cut to the core of what this issue was about – for the majority, it was less about whether they had cheated, and more about the kind of team they had become.
Anyone who had played park, grade, shield or Test cricket had a sense of where ball tampering lay on the scale of atrocities.
The loudest voices, whether they were PMs, radio hosts or bandana-clad opinionists, were those who had never played cricket at any level.
But people were fed up with that Australian side.
The impression leading into the South Africa series was of a mean, cosseted, overworked, joyless team.
It wasn’t helped by the baiting tabloids, the appalling TV coverage, the puerile marketing and the blind-eyed administration.
But the odd dick pick and stumping incident aside, there was very little scandal with the post sandpaper-gate team.
The appointment of Pat Cummins as captain was central to that.
“No sledging, no arguing, no anger, no love gone wrong, no dust ups, no bust ups,” Peter Lalor wrote in The Australian.
The usual grifters and chuckle merchants said he was too woke, and that the team was too nice.

Meanwhile, the team met every challenge, quietly disabusing the idea that cricket was somehow central to the national psyche, and that they had to behave like complete assholes to be successful at it.
But the events in Cape Town were always bubbling away.
“What’s left to come out after eight years?” Mitchell Starc asked on the eve of this year’s South African tour.
No-one, with the possible exceptions of Enid Blyton and Peter FitzSimons, write more books than Australian cricketers.
And the literary ambitions of Usman Khawaja and David Warner were always going to further fan the flames.
Hell, these days you don’t even need a book deal.
You just need sufficient distance from national duties and functioning wifi.
Warner’s thoughts were posted from Nepal, taking time out from demolition duties at the Kathmandu Gorkhas.
Khawaja has been accused of having an axe to grind, and a publishing fortune to make.
One particularly objectionable columnist wrote of “his talent for inserting race, religion and victimhood into his story”.
But the chapter on Cape Town isn’t as inflammatory as many have made out.
The most interesting and revelatory passages in the book lie elsewhere.

article.title: Andy Robertson vượt cột mốc lịch sử, khẳng định dấu ấn ở đội tuyển Scotland
article.summary: Hậu vệ Andy Robertson chuẩn bị chạm mốc 103 lần khoác áo đội tuyển Scotland, vượt qua thành tích của Kenny Dalglish và ghi dấu ấn đậm nét trong vai trò thủ lĩnh.
body: Hậu vệ Andy Robertson chuẩn bị đạt cột mốc 103 lần khoác áo đội tuyển quốc gia khi bước vào trận đấu tại St Gallen, qua đó vượt qua kỷ lục của huyền thoại Kenny Dalglish. Dù bóng đá Scotland từng sản sinh ra nhiều tên tuổi lớn ở các vị trí khác nhau trong những thập kỷ trước, hành trình vươn lên đỉnh cao của cầu thủ đang khoác áo Liverpool này mang những dấu ấn rất riêng.

Khởi đầu sự nghiệp quốc tế từ tháng 3 năm 2014 trong trận giao hữu tại Warsaw dưới tư cách cầu thủ từng bị loại khỏi hệ thống trẻ Celtic và phải làm lại từ Queen's Park lẫn Dundee United, Robertson đã không ngừng tiến bộ. Cựu huấn luyện viên Steve Bruce từng đưa anh đến Hull City đánh giá cao năng lực và tinh thần thi đấu bền bỉ của hậu vệ này, trong khi cựu đồng đội Alan Hutton cũng bày ấn tượng mạnh mẽ với nguồn năng lượng không mệt mỏi của anh trên sân.

Được trao băng đội trưởng từ năm 2018 bởi huấn luyện viên Alex McLeish, cầu thủ 32 tuổi đã đảm nhận trọng trách này trong 80 trận đấu. Dưới sự dẫn dắt của Robertson trên sân cỏ, tuyển Scotland đã chuyển mình từ một tập thể lận đận ở đấu trường quốc tế trở thành gương mặt quen thuộc tại các giải đấu lớn, đồng thời khẳng định tầm quan trọng của người thủ lĩnh đối với môi trường sinh hoạt chung của toàn đội.

article.title: U.23 Việt Nam vô địch giải giao hữu quốc tế tại Gia Lai, Minh Tâm lập cú đúp danh hiệu
article.summary: Đội tuyển U.23 Việt Nam khép lại giải giao hữu quốc tế U.23 - Gia Lai VTV Cup 2026 với chức vô địch bất bại sau trận hòa U.23 Qatar, đồng thời thâu tóm các giải thưởng cá nhân quan trọng.
body: Tối 14.11, lễ bế mạc giải bóng đá giao hữu quốc tế U.23 - Gia Lai VTV Cup 2026 đã diễn ra trên sân Pleiku, khép lại hành trình tranh tài của bốn đội tuyển gồm U.23 Việt Nam, U.23 Qatar, U.23 Singapore và U.23 Thái Lan. Thầy trò HLV Đinh Hồng Vinh chính thức đăng quang ngôi vô địch với thành tích bất bại, giành tổng cộng 7 điểm sau ba lượt trận.

Ở lượt trận đấu cuối cùng, U.23 Việt Nam có cuộc chạm trán thử thách với U.23 Qatar. Dù để đối thủ vươn lên dẫn trước trong hiệp thi đấu thứ nhất, đội chủ nhà vẫn thể hiện bản lĩnh kiên trì tổ chức lối chơi. Phút 48, tiền đạo Nguyễn Minh Tâm lập công mang về bàn thắng quân bình tỷ số 1-1, giữ vững ngôi đầu bảng cho đội nhà.

Với chức vô địch thuyết phục này, U.23 Việt Nam nhận phần thưởng trị giá 100.000 USD, tương đương khoảng 2,6 tỉ đồng. Trong khi đó, U.23 Qatar đứng vị trí á quân với 40.000 USD và U.23 Thái Lan nhận 20.000 USD cho hạng ba chung cuộc.

Bên cạnh thành tích tập thể, các cầu thủ trẻ Việt Nam còn áp đảo ở các hạng mục vinh danh cá nhân. Tiền đạo Nguyễn Minh Tâm đang khoác áo HAGL thâu tóm cú đúp danh hiệu Cầu thủ xuất sắc nhất giải và Vua phá lưới với 3 bàn thắng. Ở vị trí trấn giữ khung thành, thủ môn Cao Văn Bình cũng được bầu chọn là Thủ môn xuất sắc nhất giải nhờ những pha cứu thua ấn tượng, góp phần quan trọng vào sự chắc chắn của hàng phòng ngự U.23 Việt Nam suốt giải đấu.

article.title: Chính phủ Anh cân nhắc thảo luận về quy định độ tuổi đồng thuận tình dục
article.summary: Các bộ trưởng Anh cho biết vấn đề thay đổi độ tuổi đồng thuận tình dục sẽ được đưa ra thảo luận, sau những lời kêu gọi từ các nạn nhân trong các vụ án liên quan đến nghệ sĩ giải trí.
body: Chính phủ Anh đang đối mặt với những lời kêu gọi thay đổi khung pháp lý về độ tuổi đồng thuận tình dục. Các bộ trưởng xác nhận vấn đề này sẽ được đưa ra thảo luận trong thời gian tới, trong bối cảnh dư luận hướng sự chú ý lớn về các vụ bê bối liên quan đến giới giải trí.

Theo quy định hiện hành tại Anh, người trưởng thành ở mọi lứa tuổi đều có thể quan hệ tình dục hợp pháp với thanh thiếu niên từ 16 đến 17 tuổi. Tuy nhiên, các chiến dịch vận động và nạn nhân đã lên tiếng yêu cầu áp dụng mức độ tuổi đồng thuận theo thang bậc để ngăn chặn sự mất cân bằng quyền lực giữa người lớn tuổi và trẻ vị thành niên.

Động thái này diễn ra sau khi diễn viên hài Russell Brand bị kết án tù vì tội hiếp dâm và tấn công tình dục. Một trong những người từng tố cáo, sau khi từ bỏ quyền giấu tên, đã công khai kêu gọi nhà nước cấm các mối quan hệ tình dục giữa người trưởng thành lớn tuổi và người dưới 18 tuổi.

Nhiều chính trị gia và tổ chức bảo vệ trẻ em cũng lên tiếng ủng hộ việc mở một cuộc tranh luận công khai để xem xét lại hệ thống luật pháp hiện hành, nhằm bảo vệ nhóm vị thành niên trước nguy cơ bị thao túng hoặc lạm dụng quyền lực.

article.title: Lực lượng hậu thuẫn bởi Saudi Arabia rút lui khỏi Biển Đỏ trước đà tiến của lực lượng Houthi
article.summary: Lực lượng Vũ trang miền Nam tại Yemen tuyên bố rút lui khỏi vùng bờ biển Biển Đỏ sau nhiều tuần giao tranh, trong bối cảnh ưu thế quân sự tiếp tục nghiêng về phía lực lượng Houthi và các cuộc tấn công xuyên biên giới gia tăng.
body: Các lực lượng được Saudi Arabia hậu thuẫn tại Yemen vừa cho biết họ đang tiến hành rút quân khỏi khu vực bờ biển Biển Đỏ. Quyết định này được đưa ra sau nhiều tuần giao tranh căng thẳng nhằm giành lại quyền kiểm soát các vùng lãnh thổ chiến lược từ tay phong trào Houthi có liên kết với Iran.

Theo tuyên bố từ lực lượng Vũ trang miền Nam liên minh với chính phủ Yemen, động thái tái triển khai lực lượng nhằm mục đích bảo vệ thành phố Aden — thủ đô lâm thời của chính phủ được quốc tế công nhận trong suốt hơn một thập kỷ qua. Giới quan sát nhận định sự rút lui này là một đòn giáng mạnh đối với chính quyền Yemen và các đồng minh Saudi Arabia, khi cân bằng quyền lực tại chiến trường tiếp tục nghiêng về phía lực lượng Houthi.

Việc rút quân đồng thời thừa nhận rằng liên minh chính phủ và Saudi Arabia chưa thể giành lại quyền kiểm soát eo biển Bab al-Mandab, một tuyến hàng hải huyết mạch cho thương mại toàn cầu nằm ở phía nam Biển Đỏ. Bên cạnh đó, lực lượng Vũ trang miền Nam cho biết việc tái bố trí lực lượng cũng giúp họ tập trung giải tỏa thế bao vây của Houthi tại thành phố Taiz.

Ở diễn biến liên quan, xung đột tại đây bùng phát trở lại từ tháng 7 trong bối cảnh căng thẳng khu vực gia tăng. Trong khi đó, lực lượng Houthi tiếp tục thực hiện các cuộc tấn công bằng máy bay không người lái và tên lửa nhằm vào hạ tầng quân sự cùng cơ sở năng lượng tại Saudi Arabia, bao gồm thủ đô Riyadh và các khu vực dầu mỏ.

article.title: Israel tiêu diệt chỉ huy Lữ đoàn Rafah của Hamas trong cuộc không kích tại Gaza
article.summary: Quân đội Israel và các quan chức Hamas xác nhận Samir Abu Younis, chỉ huy mới được bổ nhiệm của Lữ đoàn Rafah thuộc Hamas, đã thiệt mạng trong một cuộc không kích tại miền nam Dải Gaza.
body: Một chỉ huy cấp cao của lực lượng Hamas vừa thiệt mạng trong một cuộc không kích của Israel tại khu định cư ở miền nam Dải Gaza. Sự việc này đánh dấu một diễn biến mới trong bối cảnh các hoạt động quân sự và đụng độ vẫn tiếp diễn tại vùng lãnh thổ này, bất chấp thỏa thuận ngừng bắn đạt được từ năm trước.

Theo thông tin từ Lữ đoàn Al-Qassam, cánh quân sự của Hamas, và được các quan chức Israel xác nhận, nhân vật thiệt mạng là Samir Abu Younis, 53 tuổi, người mới được bổ nhiệm làm chỉ huy Lữ đoàn Rafah từ ngày 15 tháng 9 sau cái chết của người tiền nhiệm Nael Abu Obeid. Vụ không kích diễn ra vào ngày thứ Bảy tại khu Al-Mawasi, nơi có nhiều người tản cư sinh sống.

Nhân chứng tại hiện trường cho biết bốn quả tên lửa đã bắn trúng một lều trại tại khu Al-Waha thuộc Al-Mawasi, gây ra hỏa hoạn. Các nguồn tin y tế tại Bệnh viện Nasser ở thành phố Khan Younis ghi nhận một thi thể và ba người bị thương được đưa tới cấp cứu sau cuộc tấn công.

Lực lượng Phòng vệ Israel (IDF) cùng cơ quan an ninh ISA ra tuyên bố xác nhận đã tiêu diệt Younis. Phía Israel cáo buộc nhân vật này là một nhân vật trung tâm trong hàng ngũ lãnh đạo của Hamas, có vai trò chỉ đạo các hoạt động tấn công nhằm vào thường dân Israel cũng như binh sĩ IDF, đồng thời nỗ lực khôi phục sức mạnh cho tổ chức vũ trang này.

Về phía Hamas, Al-Qassam Brigades khẳng định Younis từng tham gia nhiều chiến dịch và là một trong những chỉ huy quan trọng tham gia hoạch định cuộc tấn công vào miền nam Israel ngày 7 tháng 10 năm 2023. Tổ chức này đã gọi cái chết của ông là một vụ ám sát, đồng thời cho biết tang lễ sẽ được tổ chức tại Khan Younis.

Cuộc xung đột tại đây bùng phát sau sự kiện ngày 7 tháng 10 năm 2023, khiến khoảng 1.200 người thiệt mạng và 251 người bị bắt làm con tin ở miền nam Israel. Theo bộ y tế tại vùng lãnh thổ này, tổng số người thiệt mạng kể từ đó đã vượt mốc 74.650 người.

Mặc dù lệnh ngừng bắn đã được ký kết vào tháng 10 năm ngoái, Israel vẫn duy trì các cuộc không kích rải rác mà họ tuyên bố nhằm vào các tay súng Hamas còn lại. Phía Israel lập luận rằng các hành động quân sự này nằm trong quyền hạn được phép theo các điều khoản của thỏa thuận ngừng bắn.

article.title: Những người có tên độc lạ trúng cử trưởng ấp, khu vực tại Cần Thơ
article.summary: Các cá nhân có tên độc lạ từng thu hút sự chú ý trên mạng xã hội trước ngày bầu cử như ông Huỳnh Hello, ông Nguyễn Văn Bậm Trợn và bà Phan Vú Sửa đều đã chính thức trúng cử chức danh trưởng ấp, trưởng khu vực tại Cần Thơ với tỉ lệ tín nhiệm cao.
body: Chiều 15-11, thông tin từ các cơ quan chức năng tại Cần Thơ cho biết toàn bộ quá trình bầu cử trưởng ấp, trưởng khu vực nhiệm kỳ 2026 - 2031 trên địa bàn thành phố đã hoàn tất. Đợt bầu cử này ghi nhận 1.227 người trúng cử trên tổng số 1.227 ấp, khu vực, đạt tỉ lệ 100%. Trong đó, số người tái cử chiếm 77,5% và số ứng cử mới chiếm 22,5%.

Đáng chú ý, danh sách trúng cử xuất hiện một số cá nhân từng gây xôn xao trên mạng xã hội trước ngày bầu cử nhờ sở hữu những cái tên độc và lạ. Cụ thể, tại xã Tân Thạnh, ông Huỳnh Hello sinh năm 1993 đã trúng cử chức danh trưởng ấp trong nhóm các ứng viên đạt tỉ lệ phiếu bầu đều vượt mức 90%.

Tại xã Long Hưng, ông Nguyễn Văn Bậm Trợn sinh năm 1983 chính thức đảm nhận vị trí trưởng ấp Phương Hòa sau khi giành tỉ lệ phiếu bầu đạt 97,95%. Trong khi đó, tại phường Hưng Phú, bà Phan Vú Sửa sinh năm 1985 đã trúng cử trưởng khu vực Phú Thuận với tỉ lệ 94,51%.

Lãnh đạo địa phương đánh giá đằng sau những cái tên thu hút sự tò mò từ cộng đồng mạng là những người cán bộ cơ sở gần gũi với nhân dân và có năng lực thực tế. Cuộc bầu cử tại Cần Thơ đợt này cũng ghi nhận sự tham gia của đông đảo cử tri đại diện cho các hộ gia đình cùng đội ngũ nhân sự có trình độ chuyên môn đa dạng.

article.title: Dàn nghệ sĩ gạo cội trở về trường cũ hát mừng 70 năm Học viện Âm nhạc Quốc gia
article.summary: Đêm nhạc kỷ niệm 70 năm Học viện Âm nhạc Quốc gia Việt Nam đã quy tụ nhiều thế hệ nghệ sĩ, giảng viên và cựu sinh viên nổi tiếng như Thanh Lam, Mỹ Linh, Trọng Tấn, Đăng Dương cùng các giọng ca gạo cội trở về biểu diễn.
body: Khoa thanh nhạc thuộc Học viện Âm nhạc Quốc gia Việt Nam vừa tổ chức đêm nhạc mang tên "70 năm - Những thanh âm ngân mãi" vào tối 14-11, nhằm hướng tới cột mốc kỷ niệm 70 năm thành lập trường và chào mừng Ngày Nhà giáo Việt Nam 20-11. Chương trình đã quy tụ tổng cộng 28 ca sĩ, bao gồm nhiều nghệ sĩ nhân dân, nghệ sĩ ưu tú cùng các gương mặt nổi bật của âm nhạc Việt Nam qua nhiều thế hệ cùng chung vui.

Sự kiện đánh dấu màn hội ngộ đặc biệt của những tên tuổi lớn từng trưởng thành từ mái trường này như Thanh Lam, Mỹ Linh, Trọng Tấn hay Đăng Dương. Dù đã là những ngôi sao tên tuổi, khi trở lại sân khấu trường cũ, họ đều nhắc lại chặng thời gian gắn bó với Nhạc viện Hà Nội trước đây. Trong đó, Thanh Lam từng theo học đàn tỳ bà rồi chuyển sang thanh nhạc từ năm 1985, Mỹ Linh đỗ thủ khoa khoa thanh nhạc năm 1993, trong khi Trọng Tấn và Đăng Dương cũng có những ngã rẽ và hành trình gắn bó sâu đậm với các thế hệ thầy cô tại đây.

Bên cạnh các tiết mục kết hợp quen thuộc như màn song ca của Thanh Lam và Mỹ Linh hay phần trình diễn của nhóm "tam ca nhạc đỏ", đêm nhạc còn ghi dấu ấn bởi sự xuất hiện hiếm hoi của các giọng hát gạo cội. Tiết mục của ba nghệ sĩ nhân dân Quang Thọ, Dương Minh Đức và Ngọc Khang cùng sự góp mặt của NSND Hà Thủy đã mang lại không gian âm nhạc xúc động cho khán giả, tái hiện lại chặng đường sư phạm bền bỉ của ngôi trường này.

Chia sẻ về dấu mốc 70 năm, lãnh đạo khoa thanh nhạc nhấn mạnh hành trình phát triển của đơn vị gắn liền với lịch sử hình thành nền âm nhạc chuyên nghiệp hiện đại nước nhà. Đêm nhạc không chỉ là dịp để các thế hệ học trò tri ân người thầy, người cô đã gắn bó với bục giảng, mà còn là minh chứng cho sự tiếp nối truyền thống nghệ thuật qua nhiều thế hệ học viên trưởng thành từ mái trường này.

article.title: Mac Mini gắn chip M6 giảm giá sớm trên Amazon trước thềm Black Friday
article.summary: Phiên bản Mac Mini cấu hình cơ bản trang bị chip M6 hiện được giảm giá 120 USD trên Amazon, xuống còn 779 USD trong đợt khuyến mãi sớm Black Friday.
body: Các cấu hình của dòng máy Mac Mini hiện đang được giảm giá trên Amazon, khởi điểm từ 779 USD cho phiên bản cơ bản sử dụng chip M6. Mức giá này thấp hơn 120 USD so với giá bán lẻ thông thường do Apple niêm yết.

Trước đó, mẫu máy này từng gặp tình trạng khan hiếm nguồn cung kéo dài trong gần nửa đầu năm nay do thời gian chờ đợi tại các nhà bán lẻ kéo dài đến ba tháng. Tình hình chỉ cải thiện vào cuối tháng 8 khi Apple giới thiệu dòng sản phẩm mới tích hợp chip M6 hoặc M5 Pro, giúp bổ sung nguồn hàng trên thị trường.

Theo ghi nhận, nhu cầu tăng cao đột biến xuất phát từ lượng lớn người dùng quan tâm đến trí tuệ nhân tạo, những người tìm kiếm một cỗ máy bàn hoạt động liên tục với dung lượng bộ nhớ đủ để chạy các mô hình cục bộ với chi phí hợp lý. Phiên bản M6 cơ bản đi kèm 16 GB RAM, trong khi phiên bản 24 GB RAM kết hợp bộ nhớ 512 GB có giá 1,150 USD trên Amazon.

Bên cạnh đó, các lựa chọn nâng cấp dung lượng lưu trữ cao hơn đòi hỏi người mua phải đặt trực tiếp qua Apple. Đối với người dùng muốn tối ưu chi phí, Best Buy cũng cung cấp phiên bản tiền nhiệm M4 với giá 649 USD, dù dòng M6 mang lại cải tiến đáng kể về hiệu năng đồ họa cho các tác vụ xử lý trực tiếp.

article.title: Bồ Đào Nha thảm bại trong ngày mở màn kỷ nguyên hậu Cristiano Ronaldo
article.summary: Đội tuyển Bồ Đào Nha đã phải nhận thất bại nặng nề nhất trên sân nhà trong một trận đấu chính thức khi để thua Đan Mạch 1-4 tại UEFA Nations League, chỉ ít lâu sau khi Cristiano Ronaldo chính thức giải nghệ quốc tế.
body: Trận đấu tại Braga đánh dấu chương mới của bóng đá Bồ Đào Nha khi họ bước vào cuộc đối đầu với Đan Mạch mà không có sự phục vụ của Cristiano Ronaldo. Siêu sao 41 tuổi đã thông báo giải nghệ đội tuyển quốc gia sau vụ mâu thuẫn với huấn luyện viên Jorge Jesus liên quan đến việc không được lựa chọn ở các trận đấu trước đó. Dù đã giành vé vào tứ kết từ trước, đội chủ nhà vẫn đặt mục tiêu giành kết quả tốt trong ngày ra quân tại UEFA Nations League.

Trước khi trận đấu diễn ra, ban huấn luyện, cầu thủ và người hâm mộ đã có những hoạt động tri ân sâu sắc dành cho cầu thủ ghi bàn hàng đầu lịch sử đội tuyển. Toàn bộ các cầu thủ ra sân mặc áo đấu mang số 7 và tên của Ronaldo, trong khi khán giả trên khán đài giăng băng rôn tri ân đội trưởng cũ và vỗ tay tán thưởng khi trận đấu bước sang phút thứ bảy. LĐBĐ Bồ Đào Nha cũng quyết định thay đổi thiết kế số áo 7 nhằm vĩnh viễn vinh danh những đóng góp của anh.

Tuy nhiên, màn trình diễn trên sân lại gây thất vọng lớn cho người hâm mộ chủ nhà. Đan Mạch nhanh chóng chiếm thế chủ động và vươn lên dẫn trước trước giờ nghỉ giải lao nhờ pha lập công trên chấm phạt đền của đội trưởng Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg sau khi Ruben Dias để bóng chạm tay trong vòng cấm. Sang hiệp hai, tiền đạo Rasmus Hojlund tỏa sáng rực rỡ với một cú đúp ở các phút 50 và 57 để nâng tỷ số lên 3-0, khoét sâu vào những sơ hở trong hàng phòng ngự Bồ Đào Nha.

Tình hình càng trở nên tồi tệ hơn khi Joachim Andersen ghi bàn bằng đầu ở phút 75, nâng cách biệt lên bốn bàn cho đội khách và khiến nhiều cổ động viên trên sân phải bỏ về sớm trong tiếng la ó. Bàn thắng danh dự của Bernardo Silva trong thời gian bù giờ chỉ giúp định đoạt kết quả trận đấu sau khi VAR can thiệp. Thất bại 1-4 này trở thành trận thua đậm nhất trên sân nhà trong một giải đấu chính thức của Bồ Đào Nha kể từ năm 1993, đặt ra nhiều câu hỏi về năng lực thích ứng của đội bóng dưới thời HLV Jorge Jesus.

article.title: Cựu quan chức FAA: Hoãn chuyến bay là giải pháp an toàn nhất trong sự cố liên lạc
article.summary: Đại diện đội ngũ an toàn FAA Kyle Bailey cho biết việc hoãn các chuyến bay là phương án an toàn tối ưu giữa lúc xảy ra sự cố lỗi truyền thông trên quy mô toàn quốc.
body: Trong bối cảnh xảy ra sự cố gián đoạn hệ thống truyền thông trên toàn quốc tại Mỹ, cựu đại diện đội ngũ an toàn của Cục Hàng không Liên bang (FAA), ông Kyle Bailey, đã đưa ra những đánh giá về tình hình ứng phó và bảo đảm an toàn bay.
Theo quan điểm của ông Kyle Bailey, việc quyết định hoãn các chuyến bay là phương án hành động mang lại độ an toàn cao nhất trong thời điểm hệ thống gặp trục trặc bất ngờ.

Đồng thời, cựu quan chức này cũng đưa ra nhận định rằng hiện tại vẫn chưa có ai nắm bắt hoàn toàn và chính xác bản chất cũng như toàn bộ diễn biến của sự cố đang diễn ra trên hệ thống truyền thông này.
